story: As a workspace operator, I want a top-level Processes surface in the CanDoItAll shell so that process management becomes a first-class module instead of hidden inside another area.
As a project member, I want to open project-scoped processes from project UX so that process work stays anchored to the owning project.
As a developer, I want the new module to follow existing module registration patterns so that composition, DI, and migrations remain predictable.
As an architect, I want process management isolated as a canonical module so that Workbench does not absorb yet another business-owned truth model.
As a process designer, I want to create a draft process definition with name, purpose, scope, and owner so that I can iteratively model delivery flows before publishing them.
As a process designer, I want published versions to become immutable so that process runs always reference a stable definition snapshot.
As a delivery lead, I want to clone a reusable workspace template into a project so that recurring process patterns can be reused without manual recreation.
As a reviewer, I want obsolete process versions archived rather than silently overwritten so that governance and audit history remain visible.
As a CRM-HR administrator, I want process actor roles to bind to existing parties and AI-agent profiles so that durable identity stays in CRM-HR.
As a process designer, I want to assign responsible, consulted, approver, and observer roles to steps so that accountability is explicit.
As a project lead, I want to rebind a process role when a human or agent changes so that the process survives staffing changes without losing history.
As a compliance viewer, I want to inspect the provenance of actor bindings and their governance notes so that I can understand who or what was allowed to act.
As a process designer, I want to define what inputs a step requires so that downstream actors know exactly what they must receive before starting work.
As a reviewer, I want steps to declare expected outputs and evidence so that completion is validated against explicit expectations.
As an assigned actor, I want to see entry criteria, exit criteria, and expected artifacts for my step so that I do not guess what good completion means.
As a process owner, I want to capture rework guidance and contract notes on a step so that reviewers can send work back with structured expectations.
As a process designer, I want to model an explicit handoff from triage to a specialist actor so that responsibility transfer is deterministic and visible.
As a process designer, I want to define conditional branches on decision nodes so that alternate flows are encoded instead of improvised at runtime.
As an operator, I want the chosen branch and its reason recorded on a run so that I can later understand why work moved the way it did.
As an architect, I want ordered responsibilities and handoffs to exist independently of any specific runtime framework so that the process language stays stable.
As a manager, I want approval gates before sensitive or externalized work continues so that governance decisions are explicit.
As an operator, I want a run to pause awaiting approval and resume after a decision so that policy-sensitive work stays coordinated.
As a process owner, I want blocked or exceptional situations escalated to a human owner so that the process can recover instead of silently stalling.
As an architect, I want process governance metadata to map conceptually to future agent rights so that later integration does not require redesigning approvals.
As a project operator, I want to start a process run from a published process definition so that delivery work can follow an approved flow.
As an assignee, I want to claim my step and update its state so that ownership and status are visible to other actors.
As an orchestrator, I want handoff completion to activate the next eligible step so that the run progresses without hidden side effects.
As an architect, I want invalid state transitions and conflicting claims rejected so that the runtime cannot drift into ambiguous states.
As a manager, I want to inspect the full timeline of a process run so that I can see who did what, when, and why.
As an architect, I want to replay a problematic run from durable events so that I can debug handoff and state-machine failures.
As a training evaluator, I want run history to preserve step order and key decisions so that later evaluation can reason about what happened.
As a workspace user, I want major process events to appear in the shared activity stream so that process work is not operationally invisible.
As a process designer, I want an interactive canvas to model processes so that I can define flows visually instead of editing only forms or JSON.
As a process designer, I want mindmap-like grouping and flowchart-like linking so that phases, lanes, and ordered steps are legible.
As a process reviewer, I want transitions to display labels and actor context so that I can understand handoffs directly from the diagram.
As a process designer, I want saved canvas layout to reopen predictably without layout becoming the source of semantic truth so that editing stays ergonomic and safe.
As a project user, I want to jump into processes from the project modal and project board so that process work lives with other project surfaces.
As a Workbench user, I want process references and summaries projected into Workbench without moving canonical ownership there so that structure remains helpful but not authoritative.
As an architect, I want process projections to honor Workbench guardrails so that the universal node does not become a hidden canonical store.
As a project lead, I want shared-project processes discoverable by navigation rather than duplicated copies so that shared projects keep ownership of their process knowledge.
As a validation owner, I want validation gates linked to process steps so that compliance and review checkpoints can block or approve progress.
As a test owner, I want test plans and evidence attached to process steps so that process completion can reference actual proof.
As an operations user, I want overdue or blocked process work to appear as automation signals so that operational follow-up becomes visible.
As an activity user, I want process events searchable in the activity module so that I can trace process work from the shared timeline.
As a process designer, I want to import Mermaid mindmap and flowchart drafts so that existing sketches can be promoted into canonical processes.
As a process designer, I want to export process definitions as Mermaid and JSON packages so that they can be reviewed, shared, or versioned outside the UI.
As a delivery lead, I want starter process templates seeded from existing prompt-flow patterns where appropriate so that current multi-step practices are not lost.
As a template librarian, I want reusable workspace process templates managed separately from project-owned variants so that reuse does not erase local specialization.
As an architect, I want a clean AI-executor seam so that later AgentFramework integration does not require redesigning the core process module.
As a runtime designer, I want the process engine to distinguish manual, AI, and hybrid executor modes so that execution policy remains explicit.
As a process designer, I want to model AI handoffs today even before the AgentFramework runtime is embedded so that process language is not blocked by integration timing.
As a CRM-HR admin, I want AI bindings to resolve through CRM-HR and only later into an execution bridge so that identity and runtime concerns stay separated.
As a manager, I want to see bottleneck steps, approval latency, and stalled handoffs so that I can target process improvements.
As a curator, I want repeated pain points turned into structured improvement requests so that process quality can improve intentionally.
As a combined HR-manager evaluator, I want to mark training opportunities from process run patterns so that later training loops can use grounded signals.
As a process owner, I want to promote refined versions after observing real runs so that the best learned process becomes reusable.
As a local user, I want the first process-management implementation to work on SQLite so that adoption does not require infrastructure setup.
As an advanced operator, I want PostgreSQL migrations kept in step with SQLite so that larger deployments can scale without schema drift.
As an architect, I want high-volume journal data isolated behind clean contracts so that storage can later evolve without rewriting the process model.
As a team, I want predictable indexing and retention rules so that process queries stay fast as the module grows.

As a manager, I want to define reusable role templates with modality, purpose, required skills/capabilities, allocation intent, and fallback expectations so that process designers and HR start from a governed staffing archetype.
As a process designer, I want to select a role template when defining a process role so that process models reuse consistent responsibility profiles instead of ad-hoc free text.

As an HR partner, I want unresolved process roles to open linked staffing briefs or sourcing requests so that I can fulfill them through workforce, recruiting, or AI-agent sourcing without losing process context.

As a staffing coordinator, I want a role template to suggest eligible internal candidates, candidate pipelines, and AI-agent profiles based on skills, validation, and capacity so that matching starts from grounded signals.

As a process owner, I want a process role to reference a template, an eligible pool, and an optional fallback route before a concrete assignee exists so that the process can be published without pretending staffing is already solved.
As an auditor, I want published process versions and live runs to snapshot the selected role template version and resolved assignee summary so that later template edits do not rewrite history.

As an AI staffing lead, I want agent-oriented templates to capture required capabilities, validation status, human owner, and allowed execution mode so that AI staffing follows the same governance shape as human staffing.

As a compliance manager, I want approval policy to prevent self-approval and conflicting role combinations on sensitive steps so that the same actor cannot both produce and approve governed work without an explicit override.
As a staffing coordinator, I want assignment resolution to respect eligibility, capacity, and validation state so that runs do not hand work to unavailable or unapproved people or agents.
As a process owner, I want critical roles to define backup actors or fallback routes and have rebind reasons journaled so that stalled runs can recover without losing accountability.
As a process sponsor, I want every important process to have an explicit end-to-end owner, customer, and strategic objective so that accountability is not lost between departments.
As a process designer, I want to model upstream and downstream interface contracts with done definitions and required handoff data so that boundaries between processes are explicit.
As a middle manager, I want stewardship responsibilities separated from org-chart boxes so that value flow can be improved without redrawing the hierarchy.
As a portfolio manager, I want process criticality and customer type attached to each process so that modeling depth and governance can be prioritized sensibly.
As a triage lead, I want steps to validate input completeness and classification before work proceeds so that bad intake does not poison the rest of the process.
As a process owner, I want approved variants and exception paths captured explicitly so that real-world deviations are handled deliberately instead of through hidden workarounds.
As a governance lead, I want decision rights and escalation thresholds modeled explicitly so that the organization knows who may decide what and when.
As an operations lead, I want controls tagged by risk tier so that low-risk work is not buried under unnecessary approvals.
As a process analyst, I want lead time split into touch time, wait time, and blocked time so that optimization targets the real delay instead of just visible work.
As a capacity manager, I want bottlenecks and queue reasons correlated with staffing and availability so that I can see where the process really collapses.
As a customer-success lead, I want outcome metrics such as first-time-right and satisfaction linked to the process so that activity counts do not masquerade as value.
As a process owner, I want dashboards segmented by customer, interface, and criticality so that I can focus improvements where business impact is highest.
As a governance board member, I want governed change requests with impact analysis and rollout plans so that process versions do not fork unofficially.
As a middle manager, I want clear stewardship tasks and acknowledgment of major process changes so that process adoption does not stop at an executive announcement.
As a process librarian, I want criticality-based prioritization of which processes deserve deep modeling so that the organization does not over-document everything equally.
As a new participant, I want role-specific guidance and process literacy aids so that BPM concepts are usable in real work rather than extra bureaucracy.
As a quality inspector, I want to compare the modeled path with observed execution and recorded deviations so that audits reflect what people actually do.
As a process owner, I want repeated bypasses, shadow steps, and unofficial loops flagged from runtime evidence so that I can distinguish intentional variants from process breakdowns.
As a senior manager, I want field observations governed with restricted visibility so that sensitive influence patterns or workaround notes are handled responsibly.
As an improvement lead, I want deviation clusters turned into actionable change or training items so that conformance review feeds continuous improvement instead of static reporting.
As a process designer, I want executable steps to generate a normalized work brief so every human or agent receives the same scoped objective, inputs, outputs, and governance expectations.
As a triage owner, I want routing choices recorded as modeled process decisions so handoffs are explainable and governed instead of hidden inside runtime chat logic.
As a runtime operator, I want baton handoffs to be durable and replayable so I can reconstruct who passed what to whom and why.
As a senior architect, I want production agent collaboration to flow through the modeled process unless an explicit override is journaled so the process remains the canonical collaboration graph.
As a process operator, I want the same canvas to show live run state so I can see active steps, waiting points, and baton movement without stitching together multiple views mentally.
As a quality reviewer, I want runtime overlays to be clearly marked as projections so nobody mistakes canvas chrome for canonical state or edits the wrong layer.
As a manager, I want the timeline and canvas to stay in sync so I can identify the real blocking step or wait reason quickly.
As a process designer, I want published diagram layout reused for runtime overlays so modeled structure and live supervision stay visually aligned.
As a senior C# architect, I want CRM-HR to remain the canonical business template and identity source even if AgentFramework carries runtime template fields so we do not create dual registries.
As a platform owner, I want provider and capability registries to converge to CanDoItAll ownership so future AI execution uses shared configuration and proof rules.
As a QA lead, I want external AI sessions, logs, and metrics correlated back to process and step context so audits and performance reviews preserve business traceability.
As a governance owner, I want process step policy to constrain future agent permissions and approvals so runtime autonomy never bypasses modeled decision rights.
